clue.text: Puppet king holding a piece of foreign currency

indicators.note: holding means the puppet-and-king pair wraps round the next word

parts.note: a doll is a puppet or plaything
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A marionette monarch clutches a coin from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside DOLL + R, between the L and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The US unit of money is a foreign coin or note to a British solver.

clue.text: Affliction that one aches to have, monotonous though it 5 seems to be

definitions.text: Affliction that one aches to have, monotonous though it 5 seems to be

parts.words: Affliction that one aches to have, monotonous though it 5 seems to be
parts.note: an ache that is steady and dreary rather than sharp: a suffering described as both an aching and a tedious thing

explanation.walkthrough: The 'monotonous' quality is the first word, the 'affliction' felt as an ache the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent low ache is called a dull one, and an ache is a kind of bodily suffering.

clue.text: Well, it's nothing amiss in Co. Kerry

indicators.note: amiss means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of it's, ignoring the apostrophe
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone reassures a listener that all is fine down in County Kerry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amiss' rearranges WELL + ITS + O. Listowel is a market town in County Kerry, in south-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies within that Irish county, so the place is something found there.

clue.text: Prayers for our feathered friends

definitions.meaning: Ave Marias, the Hail Mary prayers
the zoological class of birds is named in Latin

explanation.definitionFit: Hail Marys are short Latin prayers, and the bird class in biology carries the Latin plural for birds.

clue.text: They do nothing but flaunt their wealth?

definitions.text: They do nothing but flaunt their wealth?

parts.words: They do nothing but flaunt their wealth?
parts.note: people of leisure with money and no work, who idle about in luxury

explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people who need not work are a leisured class living in ease.

clue.text: A cheat who trades in braces?

definitions.meaning: a two-faced trickster who deceives
a brace is a pair, so a merchant in pairs deals in doubles

explanation.definitionFit: A deceiver plays both sides; read literally, a seller of pairs is a dealer in twos.

clue.text: She's well and truly partial

indicators.note: partial means only part of the words is used, so the name sits inside them

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be in good health and genuinely biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial' signals the name inside 'wELL And'; 'truly' only joins the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a woman's first name, so it can stand for a female pronoun.

clue.text: Is about to get up, but flags

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: taken as written
to rise is to get up out of bed

explanation.surface: Someone is about to get out of bed but is flagging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' looks like a verb meaning tires, but is a noun: flag is an old name for the iris plant. 'about' places one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, so garden flags are these lily-like plants.

clue.text: Epoch-making flight made years ago across the desert

definitions.text: Epoch-making flight made years ago across the desert

parts.words: Epoch-making flight made years ago across the desert
parts.note: Muhammad's journey from Mecca to Medina in AD 622, from which the Islamic calendar is counted

explanation.definitionFit: The Prophet's escape to Medina begins the Muslim era, so it literally made an epoch.

clue.text: An edifice protected by the state, like the Tower of Pisa?

definitions.text: An edifice protected by the state
definitions.meaning: a structure on the official register of historic ..., guarded by law
... also means leaning, as a ship lists to one side

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a building of historic interest is put on a list that bars changes to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A protected historic structure is on the official register; a tilting tower lists like a ship.

clue.text: See 9
A verity not altogether to be relied on

definitions.text: A verity not altogether to be relied on

parts.words: A verity not altogether to be relied on
parts.note: a statement only part true, so trust in it is misplaced

explanation.definitionFit: A verity is a fact; one that is only half the story is misleading.

clue.text: A mere variant of billiards or snooker

definitions.meaning: a mere is a small lake or pond
a cue game on a table with pockets, played in bars

explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a pond of still water; the American cue game is another relative of snooker.

clue.text: East German city orchestra that has often played in Britain

definitions.meaning: a city on the Saale in Saxony-Anhalt, birthplace of Handel

definitions.text: orchestra that has often played in Britain
definitions.meaning: the Manchester symphony orchestra named after its German-born founder, Sir Charles

explanation.definitionFit: Handel's birthplace is in eastern Germany, and the Manchester orchestra carries its founder's surname.

clue.text: Infer a reason for apprehension

annotationWithheld.why: Infer a reason for apprehension (4): FEAR is not a run in 'Infer a' (it gives FERA), and no indicator signals a hidden word; the wordplay as held does not build the answer

clue.text: Sacks brought up to sit on, maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to sack a town is to loot it

explanation.surface: Bags carried upstairs might serve as seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns LOOTS round in this down clue. 'Sacks' looks like bags, but is the verb for plundering.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat is something one sits on, among other things.

clue.text: He's so upset about a little credit

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation goes round the following letter

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit in accounts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is so distressed over a small amount of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses its word and 'about' wraps the credit abbreviation round A. The definition is just 'He', a man's name; 'credit' tempts as the definition but is only wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a man's first name, so a male pronoun can stand for it.

clue.text: Nominally what every serving man will have

definitions.text: Nominally what every serving man will have

parts.words: Nominally what every serving man will have
parts.note: a soldier's tag stamped with his name and number, worn round the neck

explanation.definitionFit: Service personnel wear a stamped tag giving name and number, a so-called dog tag.

clue.text: Maddened by change, peremptorily asked for one's rights

indicators.note: by change means the letters of the word are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone driven wild by a reform insists on their entitlements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by change' rearranges MADDENED. 'Maddened' looks like the subject's mood, but it is only the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist firmly on something as owed is to claim it, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Incidentally, where was that roadside inn?

definitions.meaning: a phrase used to bring in a side remark
an inn on the side of a road is beside the road, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces an aside; literally it says something stands next to the road.

clue.text: King's College? A capital arts centre

definitions.meaning: a college belonging to the monarch, read literally
the London institution on Piccadilly for painters and exhibitions

explanation.walkthrough: King's College is a real Cambridge college, which is the false path; read literally it is a sovereign's school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of the crown is a regal college; the London body of artists runs exhibitions in Piccadilly.

clue.text: Rock-plant I found among S the ruins of Basra

indicators.note: found among means the single letter is placed inside the other letters
ruins means the city's name is wrecked and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant discovered growing in the wreckage of an Iraqi city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ruins of' rearranges BASRA as ARABS, and 'found among' puts I inside, before the last S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock cress is a low alpine plant grown in rock gardens.

clue.text: Old piece of silver Rudolph turned in

indicators.note: turned means the name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Rolf is a short form of the name Rudolph

explanation.surface: Someone named Rudolph handed in an antique silver coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the short name, giving FLOR. The florin was a British two-shilling coin, withdrawn after decimalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The British two-shilling coin, now withdrawn, was a silver coin.

clue.text: Keep going over a list

definitions.meaning: to keep turning over and over, as a ball does
a register of names

explanation.definitionFit: A ball keeps turning as it travels along; a register of names is read out at a roll call.

clue.text: Alliance supporter who means to get tough

definitions.meaning: David ... led the Liberals in the 1980s Liberal-SDP Alliance
to ... oneself is to harden one's resolve

explanation.walkthrough: The Alliance was the 1980s partnership of Britain's Liberal and Social Democratic parties.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal leader of the Alliance era bore this surname; the verb means to harden oneself.

clue.text: A mess — or what may be served in it, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a muddle or botch

definitions.text: what may be served in it, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a mess is also a canteen, where a chopped meat dish might be dished up

explanation.definitionFit: A botched job is a muddle; chopped meat and potato is a canteen dish served in a military mess.

clue.text: About five Rumanian coins for a Hebrew patriarch

indicators.note: about means the coins go round the numeral

parts.note: lei is the plural of leu, the Romanian currency
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Roughly five Romanian coins are paid for a Biblical forefather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like roughly, but puts V inside LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was a son of Jacob, founder of a tribe of Israel and so a forefather.

clue.text: Ruler who was expelled from 25

indicators.note: from means the letters are made from another entry, rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, a word for a mess

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch was driven out of a numbered place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges the letters of 25, HASH. The Shah of Iran was overthrown in 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Persian monarch was deposed and driven into exile.

clue.text: A grilling that is openly con-ducted

definitions.text: A grilling that is openly con-ducted

parts.words: A grilling that is openly con-ducted
parts.note: a questioning held in the open air, where the grilling is literal cooking over coals

explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor meal cooked over coals is food grilled in the open air.

clue.text: A ghost …

parts.note: a faint image or phantom, continued by the next clue where it is the dark left by blocked light

explanation.walkthrough: Read with the next clue: the ghost is what appears when daylight is blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost, and a dim trace of someone is a mere phantom of them.

clue.text: … whose absence would make the world a dull place to live in

definitions.text: … whose absence would make the world a dull place to live in

parts.words: whose absence would make the world a dull place to live in
parts.note: the light from our star, without which everything would be dim, and which casts the ghost of the previous clue

explanation.definitionFit: Daylight brightens everything; without the light from our star the world would be dim.

clue.text: Stuff that's not much good, not even to throw out?

indicators.note: out means the throw word lies outside, round the other

parts.note: to shy is to throw
a number that is not even is odd

explanation.surface: Poor material that isn't even worth discarding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' wraps the throwing word round the other. 'Stuff' is cloth: shoddy is cheap fabric made from recycled wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is cheap cloth from rag wool, so poor-quality material.
